rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: Deckers quietly renewed its backup line of credit — think of it as renewing a home equity line you almost never actually use. The credit limit went up to $500 million, the expiration was pushed out five years to 2031, and the bank fees got a little cheaper. For a company that alr
risks: If margin pressure is confirmed as structural in the next earnings print — driven by discounting rather than deliberate marketing investment — it would elevate the risk of a brand-moat erosion narrative taking hold in the market, compressing the multiple further even if FCF holds.

SG&A growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue in Q1 FY27; if this reflects a higher-cost operating model rather than investment spending, operating margins could structurally compress by 200-300bps versus thesis assumptions.

Inventory rose $320M in the quarter to $807.6M—a seasonal build but the absolute level warrants monitoring against sell-through data; any buildup into fiscal year-end would be a kill-criterion proximity signal.

Operating lease commitments surged ($120M of new ROU assets in one quarter vs. $45M prior year), indicating a significant retail or distribution footprint expansion; lease costs are fixed obligations that increase operating leverage in a downturn.

rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: Google's CEO told employees that Waymo—its self-driving car division—might start contributing real money to Alphabet's finances as early as 2027. This is encouraging but vague: no dollar figures were given, and Waymo has been burning cash for years with commercialization always f
risks: Pichai's 2027 framing could raise employee and investor expectations for Waymo that the business fails to meet, creating a credibility headwind if the timeline slips.

Remaining regulatory proceedings (notably the Search distribution antitrust case) continue and could still produce meaningful remedies, including restrictions on default search agreements with Apple and Android OEMs — this risk is unresolved and arguably more structurally significant than the ad tech case.
A future administration or appeal could revisit ad tech remedies; legal victories are durable but not always permanent in antitrust proceedings.
OpenAI's ad business, if growing 10x in six months, may be building a competing intent-based ad auction that directly competes for search advertising budgets, not just user attention.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: NVIDIA has made what's being called its biggest investment outside the US, partnering with MediaTek — a major chip company that makes processors for smartphones, cars, and smart devices. The deal could help NVIDIA get its AI software and computing capabilities into many more type
risks: Co-design partnerships with external chip companies introduce IP governance complexity and potential for roadmap misalignment if strategic priorities diverge.
A large foreign investment concentrated in Asia increases geopolitical exposure at a time when US-China technology tensions and export control regimes are active risks.
If NVIDIA pursues a pattern of large external model licenses, cumulative licensing costs could meaningfully burden FCF and signal a strategic dependency on third-party AI capabilities.
Licensing Poolside's code-generation model creates a latent conflict-of-interest risk if Poolside later competes for enterprise software contracts that NVIDIA also pursues.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: Microsoft announced it is reorganizing how it groups and reports its businesses, moving from three divisions to two starting next year: one focused on AI agents and cloud infrastructure, and one covering devices and consumer products. This is an internal accounting and reporting
risks: Reduced metric granularity: if Azure revenue growth is no longer separately reported, the primary empirical check on thesis driver #1 is weakened, making it harder to detect early share-loss signals.
Segment consolidation may obscure deterioration in the Devices/consumer businesses (Surface, Xbox, consumer Office) by blending them with higher-quality enterprise and cloud revenues.
Until Exhibit 99.1 is fully reviewed, there is uncertainty about which investor metrics will be retained, discontinued, or newly introduced in FY27.

If Okta successfully packages AI-native identity management as a best-of-breed alternative to Microsoft Entra, it could slow the 'consolidate security onto Microsoft' purchasing trend that has driven security segment outperformance — worth monitoring over 2-3 quarters.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: The US government's consumer protection regulator has sued Amazon over how it runs its advertising business. Amazon sells ads to brands that want to reach shoppers on its platform, and this is one of its most profitable businesses because Amazon knows exactly what people are shop
risks: FTC lawsuit may seek to restrict Amazon's use of first-party retail data for ad targeting, which is the core competitive advantage of the advertising segment.
Regulatory precedent from this case could invite additional state or international regulatory scrutiny of Amazon's advertising practices.
Legal costs and management distraction, while manageable for a company of Amazon's scale, add friction.
Custom silicon underperforms NVIDIA hardware for large model training workloads, forcing continued NVIDIA dependence for the highest-value AI use cases and limiting the margin benefit.

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: Meta announced a new AI model focused on coding, which briefly pushed the stock up. This fits the pattern of Meta regularly releasing open-source AI tools to stay competitive and attract developers. However, a coding model is not the same as improvements to Meta's ad targeting or
risks: The favorable outcome relative to Snap in this case may invite copycat plaintiffs or plaintiff attorneys to reprice their strategy and focus more attention on Meta in future litigation rounds.
State-level teen-safety legislation (age verification mandates, data restrictions for minors) remains an active and separate regulatory risk vector not addressed by this lawsuit's outcome.
If settlement terms include data-use restrictions or consent decree provisions, Meta's ad targeting effectiveness — the core engine of advertiser ROI — could be structurally impaired.
Uncertainty around the settlement's scope may cause management to adopt a more conservative capex posture at precisely the moment AI infrastructure investment is most competitively critical.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify just reported that its business-to-business sales volume — think brands selling wholesale to retailers or managing corporate buyer accounts — grew 76% in the most recent quarter. This matters because B2B commerce is stickier than regular consumer sales: once a business bu
risks: B2B GMV growth may reflect a low base effect and decelerate sharply in subsequent quarters, creating a misleading signal about sustainable enterprise momentum.
Larger B2B buyers may have negotiating power to compress Shopify Payments take-rates, pressuring Merchant Solutions gross margin as B2B scales.
Enterprise B2B customers often require custom SLAs and dedicated support; rapid B2B growth could increase operating costs if not carefully managed.

Affirm concentration risk: as BNPL volumes through Shopify grow, Shopify becomes more exposed to Affirm's credit quality, funding costs, and regulatory posture — a Affirm-specific shock could impair checkout conversion and merchant trust.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM announced a new mainframe computer built on cutting-edge 2nm chip technology. This is genuinely impressive engineering, but it mostly helps IBM keep the customers it already has — companies that run their most critical operations on IBM mainframes are not going to switch anyw
risks: If IBM monetizes AI-on-mainframe primarily through hardware upgrades rather than software licensing, margin accretion would be muted and the quality of incremental revenue would be lower than the thesis assumes.
Competitive response risk: AMD, Intel, and hyperscaler custom silicon teams may accelerate their own enterprise AI chip roadmaps, narrowing IBM's differentiation window.
Customer adoption risk: Mainframe customers tend to upgrade hardware on long cycles (5-7 years); near-term revenue impact may be minimal even if the technology is well-received.

Market sentiment divergence from management guidance creates the risk that when/if any guidance softening occurs, it will be disproportionately punished given elevated investor skepticism already priced into the stock.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Palantir's consulting partner PwC decided to use Palantir's AI software more broadly, which is a good sign — it means PwC finds the product valuable enough to deepen its commitment rather than walk away. This is exactly the kind of customer behavior the investment thesis is built
risks: If the PwC relationship represents a significant portion of commercial growth, it introduces indirect customer concentration risk — a deterioration in the PwC partnership or PwC's own AI strategy could disproportionately affect Palantir's commercial pipeline.

Market participants may over-index on partnership announcements as a valuation catalyst, pushing the stock further above intrinsic value and increasing the risk of a painful re-rating even if business fundamentals remain strong.
PwC-originated enterprise deals may carry lower integration depth and weaker expansion economics than direct-sold customers, which would dilute average contract quality over time.
The Ukraine/defense positioning exposes Palantir to geopolitical headline risk — if the conflict resolves or US policy shifts, associated contract pipeline could shrink rapidly.

rows.name: Lululemon Athletica Inc.
rows.last_memo: Lululemon just reported a quarter where sales in North America — its biggest and most profitable region — actually shrank compared to a year ago, while costs kept rising. That's a bad combination: you're making less money on the top line while spending more to run the business. T
risks: Americas top-line contraction in absolute dollars (not just deceleration) for the first time in recent history, raising the question of whether the US market is saturating or the brand is ceding share to Alo Yoga, Vuori, and others.

Stock-based compensation nearly tripled in H1 YoY ($50M vs $21M), a meaningful real cash cost that reduces economic earnings and warrants explanation — could signal retention pressures or restructured comp plans under new/interim leadership.

Executive leadership transition risk: CFO Meghan Frank is now serving as 'Interim Co-CEO,' implying the CEO role is in flux, which introduces strategic uncertainty during an operational inflection point.
Gross margin compression coinciding with revenue decline suggests the brand may be discounting to support volume, which would be a direct threat to the full-price sell-through thesis.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: UnitedHealth is scrapping about a third of the pre-approval checks it requires before paying for medical procedures. These pre-approvals are how the company controls which treatments it pays for — removing them means more medical bills get paid without review, which likely means
risks: Removal of 30% of prior authorizations may structurally expand MCR if high-cost service lines are included, with no immediate repricing offset available in government programs (Medicare Advantage rates are set annually).

Political/regulatory pressure appears to be forcing operational concessions — if this dynamic continues, additional cost-management tools (claims editing, network restrictions) could face similar pressure, creating a pattern risk.
Competitor response is unknown: if peers do not make equivalent concessions, UNH's cost position deteriorates relative to the industry without a corresponding competitive benefit.

Removing prior-authorization for 30% of services without demonstrated alternative utilization controls could accelerate medical cost trends and push MCR above pricing, directly triggering a kill criterion.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: Tesla just started giving actual public rides in its Cybercab — a car with no steering wheel — which is genuinely significant because the entire long-term investment case assumes Tesla eventually runs a profitable robotaxi network. That's the first concrete proof it can work in t
risks: Federal regulators (likely NHTSA) have opened a formal investigation into the Cybercab's steer-free design, which could result in operational restrictions, mandatory recalls, or redesign requirements that materially delay the robotaxi commercial timeline.

If Tesla is perceived as launching safety-critical vehicles without adequate pre-regulatory coordination, it may face a more adversarial federal oversight posture that slows future autonomous vehicle approvals across its product lineup.
If the Austin Cybercab event fails to demonstrate a credible near-term deployment path, market disappointment could accelerate a re-rating of autonomous driving option value downward.

Waymo's continued operational expansion — adding cities, rides, and potentially OEM partnerships — risks establishing a network-effect moat in urban robotaxi before Tesla is commercially deployed, reducing Tesla's ability to catch up.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: AST SpaceMobile just told investors it won't launch its commercial satellite internet service until 2027, later than previously expected. For a company with essentially no revenue today, every delay is expensive in two ways: it costs more cash (they're already burning over $1 bil
risks: Each incremental delay increases cumulative capital consumption before revenue onset, raising the risk that additional equity raises occur at dilutive prices given the stock is already down 50%.
Competitive direct-to-cell programs (notably SpaceX Starlink's T-Mobile partnership) gain relative maturity advantage with every month ASTS's commercial launch slips.
Partner mobile operators may renegotiate or reduce commitment if the commercial timeline uncertainty extends — this risk is latent but worth monitoring in the next earnings call.

A prolonged delay combined with a 50% stock drawdown may impair ASTS's ability to raise capital on acceptable terms, as equity issuance at current prices would be materially more dilutive than issuances 12 months ago.
